Drug Rehab for Xanax

In the popular imagination, drug addicts buy their drugs from corner drug dealers, in a dirty and dangerous environment. They break the law, spiral out of control, and may even get arrested. But life doesn’t always match our preconceived notions.

Prescription drugs are among the most addictive group of drugs, and more people are seeking drug rehabilitation for prescription drug addiction than ever before. Xanax, a powerful benzodiazepine, is especially addictive. If you have a problem with Xanax, drug rehab for Xanax can help you achieve the sobriety you deserve.

Xanax: A Dangerous Drug

People become addicted to Xanax in myriad ways. Some develop a problem after receiving a valid prescription from a doctor. Others take a friend’s prescription, or develop an addiction after using Xanax on a recreational basis.

It doesn’t matter how you become addicted to Xanax, and even a valid medical prescription can give rise to an addiction. Indeed, because Xanax can create a chemical dependency, it’s often legal users—not those who steal prescriptions from others—who develop an addiction.

Unfortunately, many addicts struggle to accept the notion that Xanax can be every bit as addictive as illegal drugs. After all, if a doctor prescribed a drug, how can it be dangerous? But prescription drugs are now the leading cause of injury-related deaths.

It doesn’t matter where you obtained your drugs, or even why you took them; what matters is how they affect your life. If your life has become unmanageable, or you can’t function without Xanax, you are an addict in need of drug rehab for Xanax.

How Xanax Affects Your Body

Xanax belongs to a class of drugs collectively known as benzodiazepines. These drugs can be used to control anxiety, induce a state of relaxation, and stop muscle spasms. In the short-term, you may feel highly relaxed when you use Xanax. But over time, as the addiction overtakes your body, you can suffer serious health consequences, including:

  • Benzodiazepine withdrawal syndrome, a potentially life-threatening withdrawal syndrome.
  • Loss of motivation and intelligence.
  • Temporary or permanent brain damage.
  • Organ damage.
  • Uncontrolled muscle movements.
  • Chronic muscular tension.
  • Difficulty relaxing.
  • Depression or worsening mental illness.
  • Delusions and hallucinations.

Do I Need Xanax Drug Rehabilitation?

One of the challenges of Xanax addiction is that many addicts simply do not want to admit they have a problem. Some Xanax addicts believe only illegal drugs can be addictive; others are simply uncomfortable admitting that a pill has taken control over their life.

If you’re unsure whether you need Xanax drug rehab, consider the effect Xanax has had on your life, and evaluate whether you’re able to quit. If the prospect of quitting seems daunting or impossible, it’s a sure sign you need help.

Still on the fence? Ask yourself the following questions. If you answer affirmatively to three or more, you are an addict in need of rehab:

  • Do you lie, break the law, or engage in doctor shopping to get Xanax?
  • Do you use more Xanax than prescribed by your doctor, or have you progressively increased your dose over time?
  • Do you worry you’ll never be able to quit Xanax?
  • Have friends or family asked you to quit using Xanax?
  • Do you use Xanax to feel “normal?”
  • Do you lie to yourself, or to others, about your reliance on Xanax?
  • Do you drive while under the influence of Xanax?
  • Have you endangered yourself or others because of Xanax?
  • Do you suffer from Xanax-related health or psychological problems?
  • Has your use of Xanax undermined your performance at work?
  • Have you suffered a financial loss because of your reliance on Xanax?
  • Have you been arrested, sued, or suffered other legal difficulties because of Xanax?
  • Do you prioritize Xanax over all other pursuits?
  • Have you abandoned once-beloved people or hobbies because of your use of Xanax?

Drug Rehab for Xanax

If you need drug rehabilitation for Xanax, you might feel overwhelmed, and perhaps even hopeless. Rest assured that Xanax addiction is a disease, not your fault, and not something you caused.

Proper treatment can help you get and stay sober, but trying to will yourself to sobriety—or avoiding treatment altogether—will only allow your addiction time to spiral further out of control. Some of the offerings of drug rehab for Xanax include:

  • Support for your family in the form of family visitation days, family therapy, and education programs about the disease of addiction.
  • Individual counseling that can help you better understand your addiction while nurturing healthy coping skills for managing temptation.
  • Group support, including group counseling and 12-step programs.
  • Enrichment activities.
  • A sober living environment complete with 24/7 support.
  • Medical detox support.
  • Lifestyle education on topics such as healthy eating, meditation, and the importance of exercise.

After Drug Rehabilitation

Addiction to Xanax isn’t a disease you get once and treat once. It’s a chronic medical condition that you’ll have to grapple with for the rest of your life. And that means you can never again use Xanax, since even a single pill is sufficient to reignite your addiction.

You’ll have to prepare to resist the temptation for the rest of your life, and that’s a big part of what drug rehab for Xanax teaches you. You’ll get a handle on your triggers for use, better understand why you use, and maybe even find an alternative “addiction,” such as exercise, with which to replace your addiction to Xanax.

Rehab is key to helping you defend your sobriety for the rest of your life. The journey may not be easy, and at times it may even feel impossible. But with enough commitment, you really can do it.
